edges.description: The transferred maternal inhibitor is what suppresses UGT1A1 activity in the infant.
edges.source: Placental Transfer of Maternal Serum Inhibitor
edges.target: Transient UGT1A1 Inhibition by a Serum Factor

edges.description: Inhibited UGT1A1 cannot conjugate bilirubin for excretion.
edges.source: Transient UGT1A1 Inhibition by a Serum Factor

edges.description: Unconjugated bilirubin accumulates because it cannot be conjugated.
Very high unconjugated bilirubin can cross into the brain and cause kernicterus.

nodes.description: Because of the risk of severe hyperbilirubinemia, affected infants are monitored closely during the first two weeks of life and treated with aggressive phototherapy if bilirubin approaches threshold levels, to prevent kernicterus. The condition is self-resolving as the maternal serum inhibitor clears.
Exchange transfusion in the newborn period is used if threshold bilirubin levels are reached despite phototherapy, to prevent kernicterus.
With UGT1A1 inhibited, hepatocytes cannot glucuronidate bilirubin, so unconjugated bilirubin accumulates.

evidence.snippet: Based on the original description, this syndrome presents with severe hyperbilirubinemia in the immediate newborn period and can result in kernicterus and death.

nodes.description: Bilirubin encephalopathy from very high unconjugated bilirubin; the feared outcome of untreated severe disease.

evidence.snippet: this syndrome presents with severe hyperbilirubinemia in the immediate newborn period and can result in kernicterus and death

nodes.description: Severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in the immediate newborn period that resolves as the serum inhibitor clears; survivors have no recurrence.

evidence.snippet: Based on the original description, this syndrome presents with severe hyperbilirubinemia in the immediate newborn period and can result in kernicterus and death.
Children who survive the neonatal period have no recurrence of hyperbilirubinemia

nodes.description: The inhibitor originates as a maternal gestational factor and reaches the fetus across the placenta, which is why the inhibitory activity is present at birth and wanes once placental transfer ends after delivery.
nodes.id: Placental Transfer of Maternal Serum Inhibitor

evidence.snippet: Placental transfer of maternal serum inhibitor of UGT1A1

nodes.description: An unidentified inhibitor in the serum of affected infants and their mothers suppresses UGT1A1 glucuronosyltransferase activity. The inhibitory effect declines after delivery, which is why the disorder is transient.
nodes.id: Transient UGT1A1 Inhibition by a Serum Factor

evidence.snippet: In vitro testing demonstrated that sera of affected infants and their mothers contained an unidentified inhibitor of UGT1A1 activity.
The serum inhibitory effects gradually decline after delivery and therefore this is a self-resolving condition.
